title: Discord at GDC 2026: Social SDK updates for game developers
description: Discord's GDC 2026 post lists Social SDK updates: simpler account linking, persistent messages, server-side moderation APIs and refined Rich Presence for game developers.
summary: Discord published its GDC 2026 update on March 9, 2026, focused on the Social SDK it launched the year before. The SDK lets a game connect a player's Discord account to their in-game account, so friends can see what they are playing and join more easily.

The post lists several additions. Account linking can now start from within Discord, with contextual prompts, publisher authentication across a studio's multiple titles, and native mobile linking on iOS and Android. Linked accounts get persistent message history, richer audio handling, and server-side moderation APIs so developers can use their preferred moderation services. Rich Presence gains custom display names, buttons and new activity types such as listening, watching and competing.

Discord also cites its own figure from initial integration partners: linked players show a median 25% increase in active game days and 16% longer session duration. This is a vendor claim from partner data, and the post does not describe the underlying method in the part we reviewed.
why_it_matters: For game developers, the practical change is lower integration effort for social features that many studios would otherwise build themselves: friend lists, chat history and moderation hooks. The moderation API detail matters for teams that already pay for a moderation vendor and want to keep it.

Weigh the retention figure carefully. It comes from Discord's own early partners, which are already large multiplayer titles, so a small studio should not assume the same lift. Teams evaluating community tooling can compare options in our [community chat platforms category](/software/best-community-chat-platforms-for-gaming-communities).
